title: "Assignments and grading"
editor: 
  mode: source

Your final course grade will be calculated as follows:

::: {.center-table}
| Category       | Percentage |
|----------------|------------|
| Quizzes        | 15%        |
| Problem Sets   | 10%        |
| Midterm Exam 1 | 25%        |
| Midterm Exam 2 | 25%        |
| Final exam     | 25%        |
:::

Your final letter grade will be determined based on the usual thresholds:

::: {.center-table}
| Letter Grade | Final Course Grade |
|--------------|--------------------|
| A+           | \>= 97             |
| A            | 93 - 96.99         |
| A-           | 90 - 92.99         |
| B+           | 87 - 89.99         |
| B            | 83 - 86.99         |
| B-           | 80 - 82.99         |
| C+           | 77 - 79.99         |
| C            | 73 - 76.99         |
| C-           | 70 - 72.99         |
| D+           | 67 - 69.99         |
| D            | 63 - 66.99         |
| D-           | 60 - 62.99         |
| F            | \< 60              |
:::

::: callout-warning
These thresholds will not change, and they will be applied exactly. This means that the final grades will not be curved, and a 92.99, for example, will not be rounded up to an A.
:::

## Quizzes (15%)

We will have six ten-minute in-class quizzes, which will be announced ahead of time. Grading scheme to be determined.

::: callout-note
## Grace

Lowest scores.... will be dropped (to be determined)
:::

## Problem Sets (10%)

Mathematics is like everything else in life; if you practice, you improve. As such, the problem sets are really the heart of the course. They must be handwritten either on paper or on a tablet and uploaded to Gradescope as a single `.pdf` file. Grading scheme to be determined.

::: callout-note
## Grace

Your lowest problem set score will be dropped at the end of the semester.
:::

## Exams (25% each)

There will be three exams. The dates, times, and locations are firm, so mark your calendar now:

-   **Midterm 1**: Tuesday October 6 during lecture;
-   **Midterm 2**: Thursday November 19 during lecture;
-   **Final**: Thursday December 10 from 2 PM - 5 PM in Gross Hall 103.

These will be old school, pencil-and-paper, in-class exams. Exams are closed-book and closed-notes. No online or electronic resources are permitted. 

If you seek testing accommodations, make sure the Student Disability Access Office sends me a letter, and then please make your appointments in the [Testing Center](https://testingcenter.duke.edu) as soon as possible.

::: callout-note
## Grace

If you do better on the final exam than you did on one of the midterms, we will replace your lowest midterm exam score with your final exam score.
:::

::: callout-warning
## No make-up exams

If you are absent from one of the midterms for whatever reason, there will not be a make-up. Pursuant to the above policy, we will simply replace the missed midterm score with the final exam score. If you miss the final exam, you get a zero unless you have a [Dean's Excuse](https://trinity.duke.edu/undergraduate/academic-policies/final-exams-scheduling-conflicts-and-absences).
:::
